claim: The method is the first that allows 3D interrogation of whole, live, untwisted nematodes at arbitrary timepoints in embryogenesis.
source: While embryo elongation has been examined before (Priess and Hirsh, 1986), our method is the first that allows 3D interrogation of whole, live, untwisted nematodes at arbitrary timepoints in embryogenesis (Figure 3, Video 2).
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the method.

claim: The strong qualitative similarities in seam cell nuclear trajectories among the five embryos led to investigation of whether data from different embryos could be combined to yield a composite model.
source: The strong qualitative similarities in seam cell nuclear trajectories among the five embryos we inspected led us to investigate whether data from different embryos could be combined to yield a composite model of development representing growth in an 'average' embryo.
evidence: This describes the rationale for creating a composite model.

claim: Except for a relative shift in time, the axial seam cell nuclear trajectories displayed very similar shapes.
source: Initial examination of the axial (nose-to-tail) seam cell nuclear trajectories from different embryos suggested a high degree of stereotypy; except for a relative shift in time, the trajectories displayed very similar shapes (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is an observation from comparing trajectories across embryos.

claim: A three parameter logistic function was used to fit the raw axial displacement data.
source: We determined the amount of shift by using a three parameter logistic function to fit the raw axial displacement data (Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Tables 1, 2, Materials and methods), overlaying the data from various embryos until the inflection points in each curve were identical.
evidence: This describes the method used for temporal alignment.

claim: Seam cell nuclear positions followed similar trajectories throughout elongation.
source: We applied the same time shift to the X- and Y- seam cell nuclear coordinates, finding that seam cell nuclear positions followed similar trajectories throughout elongation (average SD calculated across all 20 seam cell nuclei and all timepoints, <<σX>time>seam cell 0.8 µm, <<σY>time>seam cell 0.7 µm, <<σZ>time>seam cell 4.6 µm, see also Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Table 1, and 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a finding from the temporal alignment and averaging procedure.

claim: The average standard deviation across all 20 seam cell nuclei and all timepoints was 0.8 µm for X coordinates.
source: We applied the same time shift to the X- and Y- seam cell nuclear coordinates, finding that seam cell nuclear positions followed similar trajectories throughout elongation (average SD calculated across all 20 seam cell nuclei and all timepoints, <<σX>time>seam cell 0.8 µm, <<σY>time>seam cell 0.7 µm, <<σZ>time>seam cell 4.6 µm, see also Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Table 1, and 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a quantitative measure of variability.

claim: The average standard deviation across all 20 seam cell nuclei and all timepoints was 0.7 µm for Y coordinates.
source: We applied the same time shift to the X- and Y- seam cell nuclear coordinates, finding that seam cell nuclear positions followed similar trajectories throughout elongation (average SD calculated across all 20 seam cell nuclei and all timepoints, <<σX>time>seam cell 0.8 µm, <<σY>time>seam cell 0.7 µm, <<σZ>time>seam cell 4.6 µm, see also Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Table 1, and 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a quantitative measure of variability.

claim: The average standard deviation across all 20 seam cell nuclei and all timepoints was 4.6 µm for Z coordinates.
source: We applied the same time shift to the X- and Y- seam cell nuclear coordinates, finding that seam cell nuclear positions followed similar trajectories throughout elongation (average SD calculated across all 20 seam cell nuclei and all timepoints, <<σX>time>seam cell 0.8 µm, <<σY>time>seam cell 0.7 µm, <<σZ>time>seam cell 4.6 µm, see also Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Table 1, and 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a quantitative measure of variability.

claim: The three-parameter logistic function gave the best qualitative and quantitative agreement with the axial displacement data.
source: Amongst the various three-parameter sigmoidal functions (Table 2), we found that the three-parameter logistic function gave the best qualitative and quantitative (Figure 4—figure supplement 2) agreement with the data.
evidence: This is a finding from comparing different fitting functions.

claim: Fitted values were within 1.5 µm of the X, Y averaged data.
source: Despite the ad hoc nature of these fits, we found that fitted values were within 1.5 µm of the X, Y averaged data, and within 7.5 µm of the Z averaged data (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a measure of the quality of the fits.

claim: Fitted values were within 7.5 µm of the Z averaged data.
source: Despite the ad hoc nature of these fits, we found that fitted values were within 1.5 µm of the X, Y averaged data, and within 7.5 µm of the Z averaged data (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a measure of the quality of the fits.

claim: The total length of the untwisted embryo at the final time point was 162.0 ± 18.7 µm.
source: For reference, the total length of the untwisted embryo at the final time point was 162.0 ± 18.7 µm (mean ± SD, 5 embryos), measured from the nose to the last pair of seam cells, and the corresponding diameter at the last time point 16.1 ± 1.3 µm, measured at the widest cross-section in the animal.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement of embryo size.

claim: The diameter of the untwisted embryo at the last time point was 16.1 ± 1.3 µm.
source: For reference, the total length of the untwisted embryo at the final time point was 162.0 ± 18.7 µm (mean ± SD, 5 embryos), measured from the nose to the last pair of seam cells, and the corresponding diameter at the last time point 16.1 ± 1.3 µm, measured at the widest cross-section in the animal.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement of embryo size.

claim: The distance between the origin and nuclei of seam cell pair H0 changed from 2.4 µm to 23.8 µm over elongation.
source: For example, the distance between the origin and nuclei of seam cell pair H0, measured from the fitted data, changed from 2.4 µm to 23.8 µm over elongation (Figure 5B),
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the fitted data.

claim: The distance between seam cell nuclear pairs V6 and T remained essentially constant, at 22.5 µm.
source: while the distance between seam cell nuclear pairs V6 and T remained essentially constant, at 22.5 µm (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the fitted data.

claim: The rate of increase in distance between the origin and H0 was significantly greater than the increase in distance between V6 and T.
source: Thus, the rate of increase in distance between the origin and H0 was significantly greater than the increase in distance between V6 and T, over the same period.
evidence: This is a comparison of rates derived from the data.

claim: Other adjacent nuclear pairs separated at roughly similar rates from start to end of elongation, increasing in distance 6.8 ± 2.8 µm.
source: Other adjacent nuclear pairs separated at roughly similar rates from start to end of elongation (these pairs increased in distance 6.8 ± 2.8 µm, mean ± SD from 7 adjacent pairs of seam cell nuclei, again derived from the fitted data in Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the fitted data.

claim: The apparent differences in X- and Z- pre- and post-elongating seam cell nuclei positions are consistent with the asymmetric morphology of the pre-elongating embryo.
source: The apparent differences in X- and Z- pre- and post-elongating seam cell nuclei positions that we observe are consistent with the asymmetric morphology of the pre-elongating embryo.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed positional differences.

claim: Since the embryo starts out in a tadpole-like shape with the head larger than the tail, the seam cell nuclei in the head must move a greater distance than the nuclei in the tail to achieve a uniform diameter in the elongated embryo.
source: Since the embryo starts out in a tadpole-like shape with the head larger than the tail, the seam cell nuclei in the head must move a greater distance than the nuclei in the tail to achieve a uniform diameter in the elongated embryo.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the initial and final morphology.

claim: Embryo elongation is thought to be dependent on an actin-based contractile mechanism.
source: Embryo elongation is thought to be dependent on an actin-based contractile mechanism (Priess and Hirsh, 1986).
evidence: This is a statement about existing models, supported by citation.

claim: The complex, position-dependent motion observed is likely inconsistent with a simple, uniform contraction.
source: The complex, position-dependent motion we observed is likely inconsistent with a simple, uniform contraction, as this phenomena cannot explain our finding that different regions of the embryo elongate at markedly different rates.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data in relation to existing models.

claim: Current models of embryo elongation have not taken into account the differential elongation observed across the worm body.
source: To our knowledge, current models of embryo elongation have not taken into account the differential elongation we observed across the worm body.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of existing models.

claim: Incorporating additional data derived from cell positions and subcellular markers would help further refine existing models of embryo elongation.
source: We expect that incorporating additional data derived from cell positions and subcellular markers (especially cytoskeletal [Priess and Hirsh, 1986; Gally et al., 2009]) in the embryo would help further refine existing models (Ciarletta et al., 2009) of embryo elongation.
evidence: This is a speculation about future work, supported by citations.

claim: Four of the five embryos used in constructing the seam cell model had neuronal cell bodies marked with a pceh-10::GFP construct.
source: Four of the five embryos used in constructing our seam cell model also had neuronal cell bodies marked with a pceh-10::GFP construct; neurons included AIYL/R, CANL/R, and ALA.
evidence: This describes the strains used for neuronal tracking.

claim: The axial motion of neurons was qualitatively similar to the seam cell nuclei and could be well described by the three parameter logistic function.
source: The axial motion of these neurons was qualitatively similar to the seam cell nuclei and could be well described by the three parameter logistic function.
evidence: This is a finding from analyzing neuronal motion.

claim: The lateral motion of CANs could not be easily described by a simple function.
source: However, their XY motion appeared different than the seam cell nuclei. For example, the lateral motion of CANs could not be easily described by a simple function, so we used a 50 point smoothing of the averaged data as our 'fit'.
evidence: This describes a challenge in fitting CAN motion.

claim: The ALA X motion was better described by a 4th degree polynomial than a power law.
source: The ALA X motion was better described by a 4th degree polynomial than a power law, so we used the former function to fit the data (Figure 4—figure supplement 4, Table 1).
evidence: This describes the fitting approach for ALA motion.

claim: The motion of ALA and CANs was considerably more variable between datasets than the seam cell nuclei.
source: Finally, the motion of ALA and CANs (especially CANL) were considerably more variable between datasets than the seam cell nuclei (Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Supplementary files 2,3,4).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing variability across cell types.

claim: It is currently unclear whether the variability in ALA and CAN motion is strain-dependent or reflects underlying biology.
source: While it is currently unclear whether this variability is strain-dependent or reflects underlying biology, this observation underscores the need to study multiple embryos and assess the degree to which cellular motion is stereotyped in elongating embryos.
evidence: This acknowledges uncertainty about the source of variability.

claim: ALA is a single neuron with a cell body located in the dorsal portion of the head.
source: ALA is a single neuron with a cell body located in the dorsal portion of the head; a pair of long neurites extend ventrally from this cell body into the nerve ring, and then turn and extend posteriorly along the lateral nerve cord (White et al., 1986).
evidence: This is a description of ALA morphology, supported by citation.

claim: A pair of long neurites extend ventrally from the ALA cell body into the nerve ring, and then turn and extend posteriorly along the lateral nerve cord.
source: ALA is a single neuron with a cell body located in the dorsal portion of the head; a pair of long neurites extend ventrally from this cell body into the nerve ring, and then turn and extend posteriorly along the lateral nerve cord (White et al., 1986).
evidence: This is a description of ALA morphology, supported by citation.

claim: ALA neurite outgrowth continued to occur for ~240 min after the other cells assumed their final positions at the end of elongation.
source: Aligning the fitted neurites to our reference embryo allowed inspection of ALA neurite growth in the context of the elongating embryo (Figure 6A, Videos 5,6), revealing that neurite outgrowth continued to occur for ~240 min after the other cells assumed their final positions at the end of elongation.
evidence: This is a finding from tracking ALA neurite growth.

claim: The authors are unaware of any other work that has modeled the growth and positions of neurites in the post-twitching embryonic regime.
source: We are unaware of any other work that has modeled the growth and positions of neurites in the post-twitching embryonic regime (for C. elegans or any other model organism).
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the work.

claim: The C. elegans cell lineage is invariant.
source: The C. elegans cell lineage is invariant (Sulston et al., 1983), and tracking cells in the L1 larva has revealed that cellular positions in post-hatching animals are relatively stereotyped (Long et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a well-established fact about C. elegans, supported by citation.

claim: Tracking cells in the L1 larva has revealed that cellular positions in post-hatching animals are relatively stereotyped.
source: The C. elegans cell lineage is invariant (Sulston et al., 1983), and tracking cells in the L1 larva has revealed that cellular positions in post-hatching animals are relatively stereotyped (Long et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the literature.

claim: Positional stereotypy extends to the cells in the late embryo.
source: Our work suggests that this positional stereotypy extends to the cells in the late embryo as well.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the authors' data.

claim: In the case of cells or structures which actively migrate, such as the CAN neurons and ALA neurites, there seems to be greater variability in terms of end position and growth rate.
source: However, we also found that in the case of cells or structures which actively migrate, such as the CAN neurons and ALA neurites, there seems to be greater variability in terms of end position and growth rate.
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis.

claim: Some variability in temporal shifts may be due to embryos being at slightly different ages when imaging began.
source: Some of this variability may be due to relatively mundane explanations: embryos were at slightly different ages when imaging began, and temperature was moderately controlled (to within 2 to 3°C both during imaging and strain growth).
evidence: This is a speculation about sources of variability.

claim: Temperature was moderately controlled (to within 2 to 3°C both during imaging and strain growth).
source: Some of this variability may be due to relatively mundane explanations: embryos were at slightly different ages when imaging began, and temperature was moderately controlled (to within 2 to 3°C both during imaging and strain growth).
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions.

claim: Intrinsic developmental variability, caused by maternal effects or exposure to imaging could have played a role in the slightly different patterns of development observed across embryos.
source: Intrinsic developmental variability, caused by maternal effects or exposure to imaging could also have played a role in the slightly different patterns of development we observed across embryos.
evidence: This is a speculation about sources of variability.

claim: Expanding the work to other migrating and non-migrating neurons should make clear whether there is a difference in positional variability between migrating and non-migrating cells.
source: Expanding the work we describe here to other migrating and non-migrating neurons should make clear whether there actually is a difference in positional variability between migrating and non-migrating cells.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future work.

claim: Adding additional data to the 4D model is conceptually straightforward.
source: Adding additional data to our 4D model is conceptually straightforward: strains with distinguishable neurons can be crossed into the untwisting background, untwisted, trajectories of cells and outgrowths fitted, and subsequently registered with previously derived data.
evidence: This describes a potential workflow for expanding the atlas.

claim: The untwisting and annotation plugin is designed to be flexible.
source: Our untwisting and annotation plugin is designed to be flexible, so that it can be applied to most problems involving tracking position and morphology of distinguishable structures in the nematode embryo.
evidence: This describes a design feature of the software.

claim: The core of the plugin relies on defining the sides of the worm embryo.
source: The core of the plugin relies on defining the sides of the worm embryo; although our work uses a specific set of markers, we note that any other markers which define the edges of the worm body should also work.
evidence: This describes the key requirement for the untwisting algorithm.

claim: Any markers which define the edges of the worm body should work with the plugin.
source: The core of the plugin relies on defining the sides of the worm embryo; although our work uses a specific set of markers, we note that any other markers which define the edges of the worm body should also work.
evidence: This is a statement about the generalizability of the method.

claim: The annotation capability is flexible and based on manual annotation.
source: The annotation capability is also flexible; as it is based on manual annotation, almost any distinct structure can be annotated.
evidence: This describes a feature of the software.

claim: The untwisting algorithm is compatible with other high-resolution imaging methods.
source: Finally, while the isotropic resolution of the diSPIM is very helpful in resolving fine embryonic detail (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), our untwisting algorithm is compatible with other high-resolution imaging methods.
evidence: This is a statement about the generalizability of the method.

claim: The authors used a super-resolution two-photon instant structured illumination microscope (2P ISIM) to image and untwist a bent L2 larval worm.
source: For example, we used a super-resolution two-photon instant structured illumination microscope (2P ISIM) (Winter, 2014) to image and untwist a bent L2 larval worm, obtaining clear images of this relatively large specimen (Figure 1—figure supplement 4, Video 7).
evidence: This describes an application of the method to a different imaging modality.

claim: The plugin is designed specifically for untwisting nematode embryos.
source: Our plugin is designed specifically for untwisting nematode embryos, and as such is unlikely to be immediately applicable to other biological systems without substantial modification (we know of few non-nematode systems that have the same vermiform shape and degree of twisting and movement).
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the method's applicability.

claim: The concept of aligning and pooling information derived from different datasets to generate an overall 4D view of development is likely applicable to more systems than just the worm.
source: However, some of the more general concepts we implement, such as the benefit of aligning and pooling information derived different datasets to generate an overall 4D view of development, are likely applicable to more systems than just the worm.
evidence: This is a statement about the broader applicability of the conceptual approach.

claim: Automated lattice-building assumes the embryo has 20-22 seam cell nuclei.
source: Automated lattice-building assumes the embryo has 20-22 seam cell nuclei on which the lattice is based; in early periods of elongation (especially the 1.5- to 2-fold transition) expression is absent in some seam cell nuclei, requiring manual lattice-building.
evidence: This describes a limitation of the automated approach.

claim: In early periods of elongation (especially the 1.5- to 2-fold transition) expression is absent in some seam cell nuclei, requiring manual lattice-building.
source: Automated lattice-building assumes the embryo has 20-22 seam cell nuclei on which the lattice is based; in early periods of elongation (especially the 1.5- to 2-fold transition) expression is absent in some seam cell nuclei, requiring manual lattice-building.
evidence: This describes a limitation of the automated approach.

claim: Time spent in editing automatic segmentation and lattice generation results in ~8 hr of manual work when untwisting an embryo spanning 100–150 timepoints.
source: In addition, time spent in editing automatic segmentation and lattice generation results in ~8 hr of manual work when untwisting an embryo spanning 100–150 timepoints.
evidence: This describes the time required for manual work.

claim: Fully automated untwisting is not currently feasible.
source: Fully automated untwisting is not currently feasible, but the development of alternative markers may enable this goal.
evidence: This is a statement about current limitations.

claim: The development of alternative markers may enable fully automated untwisting.
source: Fully automated untwisting is not currently feasible, but the development of alternative markers may enable this goal.
evidence: This is a speculation about future improvements.

claim: The data are of sufficient quality to segment morphology in an untwisted animal.
source: While our data are of sufficient quality to segment such morphology in an untwisted animal (Figure 6—figure supplement 2, Video 8), the general question about how to combine morphological segmentations from distinct, untwisted embryos remains.
evidence: This is a statement about data quality.

claim: The general question about how to combine morphological segmentations from distinct, untwisted embryos remains.
source: While our data are of sufficient quality to segment such morphology in an untwisted animal (Figure 6—figure supplement 2, Video 8), the general question about how to combine morphological segmentations from distinct, untwisted embryos remains.
evidence: This identifies an open question.

claim: New methods developed for pre-twitching embryos may prove useful in combining morphological segmentations.
source: New methods developed for pre-twitching embryos may prove useful in this regard (Santella et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculation about potential solutions, supported by citation.

claim: Most fluorescent strains label multiple neurons that are too close in space and time to be easily resolved.
source: Most fluorescent strains label multiple neurons that are too close in space and time to be easily resolved – possible strategies to 'separate' these neurons might include 'Brainbow' (Livet et al., 2007) (spectral separation of densely labeled neurons) or heat-shock-based approaches (Halfon et al., 1997; Bacaj and Shaham, 2007) (temporal separation of densely labeled cells).
evidence: This describes a challenge in imaging, with citations to potential solutions.

claim: Possible strategies to 'separate' densely labeled neurons include 'Brainbow' (spectral separation) or heat-shock-based approaches (temporal separation).
source: Most fluorescent strains label multiple neurons that are too close in space and time to be easily resolved – possible strategies to 'separate' these neurons might include 'Brainbow' (Livet et al., 2007) (spectral separation of densely labeled neurons) or heat-shock-based approaches (Halfon et al., 1997; Bacaj and Shaham, 2007) (temporal separation of densely labeled cells).
evidence: This suggests potential solutions, supported by citations.

claim: The identity of neurons will need to be verified even if strains with sparse labeling are built.
source: Even if such strains are built, the identity of the resulting neurons will need to be verified.
evidence: This identifies a necessary step in future work.

claim: Lineaging in C. elegans has been carried out to just before twitching begins.
source: As lineaging (Bao, 2006) in C. elegans has been carried out to just before twitching begins (Giurumescu et al., 2012), in principle neurons can be identified by matching early expression to lineage data.
evidence: This is a statement about existing work, supported by citations.

claim: In principle neurons can be identified by matching early expression to lineage data.
source: As lineaging (Bao, 2006) in C. elegans has been carried out to just before twitching begins (Giurumescu et al., 2012), in principle neurons can be identified by matching early expression to lineage data.
evidence: This is an inference about how to identify neurons.

claim: If expression turns on after twitching, lineaging would need to be extended into the post-twitching regime.
source: If expression turns on after twitching, lineaging would also need to be extended into the post-twitching regime.
evidence: This is a logical consequence for identifying late-expressing neurons.

claim: 'Deep lineaging', or tracking the coordinates of all nuclei through twitching would be a valuable and complementary effort to untwisting.
source: Such 'deep lineaging', or tracking the coordinates of all nuclei through twitching would be a valuable and complementary effort to untwisting.
evidence: This is a statement about the value of complementary approaches.

claim: For almost all strains (except DCR4209 which contained membrane-targeted mCherry), fluorescent proteins were expressed cytoplasmically.
source: Finally, we note that the expression pattern of fluorescent proteins within individual neurons could be further optimized. For almost all strains (except DCR4209 which contained membrane-targeted mCherry), fluorescent proteins were expressed cytoplasmically.
evidence: This describes the expression pattern in the strains used.

claim: An improved strategy would combine cytoplasmic labeling with membrane targeting.
source: An improved strategy would combine such cytoplasmic labeling with membrane targeting, better filling out very thin neuronal outgrowths that otherwise might be missed due to low expression; a similar strategy was adopted in super-resolution microscopy to trace thin neurites (Lakadamyali et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a suggestion for improvement, supported by citation.
